content: Crofelemer is an antidiarrheal medication specifically indicated for the treatment of noninfectious diarrhea in patients with HIV/AIDS who are undergoing antiretroviral therapy. The recommended dosage is 125 mg taken orally twice daily. It has also been granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of short bowel syndrome, although its safety and efficacy in patients under 18 years of age have not been established. Crofelemer has the potential to interact with various medications by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, as well as certain transporters such as MRP2 and OATP1A2, at concentrations expected in the gastrointestinal tract. However, due to its minimal systemic absorption, it is unlikely to inhibit these enzymes or transporters systemically. These interactions can lead to increased plasma levels or effects of co-administered drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, necessitating caution, monitoring, or dosage adjustments. For example: Lonafarnib: Crofelemer may increase its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor for arrhythmias or cardiac events. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Crofelemer may increase sulbactam levels by inhibiting active secretion via OATP1. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Alfuzosin, Alprazolam, Ambrisentan, Amiodarone, Apixaban, Aprepitant, Aripiprazole, Armodafinil, Atazanavir, Atogepant, Atorvastatin, Avapritinib, Axitinib, Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens, Bedaquiline, Benzphetamine, Bosentan, Bosutinib, Bromocriptine, Budesonide, Buprenorphine (including buccal formulations), Buspirone, Busulfan, Cabozantinib, Calcitriol, Carbamazepine, Chenodiol, Chlordiazepoxide, Chloroquine, Chlorpheniramine, Cilostazol, Citalopram, Clarithromycin, Clonazepam, Clorazepate, Colchicine, Conjugated Estrogens (including vaginal formulations), Crizotinib, Cyclophosphamide, Cyclosporine, Dantrolene, Dapsone, Darifenacin, Darunavir, Dasatinib, Dexamethasone, Diazepam, Disopyramide, Dronedarone, Efavirenz, Eletriptan, Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF, Eplerenone, Ergoloid Mesylates, Ergotamine, Erlotinib, Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, stearate), Esomeprazole, Estradiol, Estrogens (synthetic conjugated), Estropipate, Eszopiclone, Ethosuximide, Etoposide, Etravirine, Exemestane, Felbamate, Felodipine, Fenofibrate, Fexofenadine, Finererone, Flibanserin, Flurazepam, Flutamide, Fosamprenavir, Fosaprepitant, Haloperidol, Imatinib, Indinavir, Isavuconazonium Sulfate, Isosorbide Dinitrate, Isosorbide Mononitrate, Isradipine, Ivacaftor, Lapatinib: Crofelemer may increase the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 or related transporters. Use caution, monitor closely, and adjust therapy as needed. In some cases, such as with Finererone, serum potassium levels should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments, and finererone dosage should be modified as necessary. For drugs like Flibanserin, co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects. In summary, while crofelemer is minimally absorbed systemically, its potential to inhibit CYP3A4 and certain transporters in the gut necessitates careful consideration of drug interactions. Close monitoring and appropriate adjustments to therapy are recommended when co-administering crofelemer with other medications metabolized by these pathways.
